$schema.description: Where the JSON Schema of this file is, for the editor.

language.description: The language of the interface: "en" (English), "pt-BR" (Brazilian Portuguese), or "system", which follows the language of the computer and falls back to English when Noren does not have it.

theme.description: The id of the theme, such as "noren-dusk". "system", or no value, follows the light or dark scheme of the system. An id Noren does not have also follows the system.

effect.description: What the system paints behind the window: "mica" or "acrylic" on Windows 11, "vibrancy" on macOS, "none" for a plain opaque window. A system that cannot paint the effect keeps the window opaque.

opacity.description: How opaque the interface is, from 0.3 (it lets most of what is behind the window through) to 1 (solid). Without a value (or null) the window is solid, and with an effect on it takes the opacity of the theme.

window.description: The window itself: the effect behind it and how opaque the interface is.

image.description: A picture file on this computer shown behind the terminals: an absolute path, or a path inside the config folder of the app (such as backgrounds/sky.jpg). A web address is refused. null shows no picture, even where the theme has one. The picture of a space wins over this one.

opacity.description: How much of the picture shows, from 0 (none) to 1 (solid). Without a value (or null) the theme says.

blur.description: How much the picture is blurred, in pixels. Without a value (or null) the theme says (none).

position.description: Which side of the window the sidebar is on.

width.description: Width of the sidebar in pixels.

compact.description: Compact mode: the sidebar leaves the layout and shows over it when the pointer touches the edge of the window.

keepOpen.description: In compact mode, keeps the sidebar open instead of hiding it.

density.description: How much room the rows of the sidebar take.

tabs.description: Where the tabs are: the tree in the sidebar, or a bar above the terminal.

paneHeaders.description: Shows a header with the title and the buttons on every pane of a tab.

appearance.description: How the window looks and is laid out.

family.description: The fonts of the terminal, by name, separated by commas: the first one found on this computer is used, such as "Cascadia Code, Consolas, monospace". Only names of font families are accepted (a web address, a semicolon or a brace is an error).
family.default: Cascadia Mono, Consolas, DejaVu Sans Mono, monospace

size.description: The size of the text in pixels. Ctrl+= and Ctrl+- change it for the open window, and Ctrl+0 goes back to this size; they do not change the file.

lineHeight.description: The height of a row of text, as a multiple of the font size. 1 is the tightest the terminal can draw.

ligatures.description: Joins the characters that a programming font draws as one sign (for example => or !=). Accepted, but it has no effect yet: the terminal draws every character on its own.

scrollback.description: How many lines the terminal keeps above the screen, from 0 (none) to 100,000. Every line takes memory in every terminal that is open.

bell.description: What the terminal does when a program rings the bell: "none", "visual" (the pane flashes), "sound" (a short beep) or "both". The tab is marked as unread whichever it is.

saveScrollback.description: Keeps the last 2,000 lines of every pane when Noren closes and every minute while the pane is in use, and shows them again, dimmed, when the pane opens. false never saves any scrollback, in any space, and removes the files already saved. A space can turn it off for itself too.

screenReaderMode.description: Turns on the screen reader support of the terminal: it keeps a hidden copy of the text on screen that a screen reader (NVDA, VoiceOver, Narrator) can read, and reads new output as it arrives. It makes the terminal slower, so it is off by default. A change reaches the terminals that are open at once.

terminal.description: The terminal: its font, cursor, scrollback, bell and screen reader support.

mods.description: The CSS files of the mods folder (next to this file) that are turned on for every space, as file names such as "compact-tabs.css", in the order they are applied: the last one wins. A file that is not in the folder is ignored.

kind.description: What the profile opens: "shell" (the default) starts a program on this machine, "ssh" opens a shell in a norend on another machine through ssh.

id.description: The id of the profile, such as "dev-shell". Unique among the profiles.

name.description: The name shown in the command palette.

program.description: The program that starts the shell, such as "pwsh.exe" or a full path. %NAME% is replaced by the environment variable NAME when a session starts. In an SSH profile it runs on the other machine, nothing in it is replaced, and when left out it is the login shell of the user there.

args.description: The arguments of the program, one item each.

cwd.description: The folder a session of this profile starts in, unless the space or the tab names one. %NAME% is replaced by the environment variable NAME. In an SSH profile it is a folder on the other machine, taken as written, and when left out the home folder of the user there.

kind.description: What the profile opens: "shell" (the default) starts a program on this machine, "ssh" opens a shell in a norend on another machine through ssh.

id.description: The id of the profile, such as "dev-shell". Unique among the profiles.

name.description: The name shown in the command palette.

host.description: The machine to reach with ssh: a host name or an address (letters, digits, ".", "-", "_" and ":").

user.description: The user to log in as. When left out ssh decides: its own configuration, then the name of the user on this machine.

port.description: The port of the ssh server. 22, or what the ssh configuration says, when left out.

identityFile.description: The private key to log in with, as a path; only this key is offered. When left out ssh tries its own keys and the agent. A key with a passphrase works only through an agent: Noren never asks for a passphrase and stores none. %NAME% is replaced by the environment variable NAME.

knownHostsFile.description: The file with the keys of the hosts you trust, as a path. When left out the known_hosts file of the user is used. A host that is not in the file is refused, never accepted on the first visit. %NAME% is replaced by the environment variable NAME.

program.description: The program that starts the shell, such as "pwsh.exe" or a full path. %NAME% is replaced by the environment variable NAME when a session starts. In an SSH profile it runs on the other machine, nothing in it is replaced, and when left out it is the login shell of the user there.

args.description: The arguments of the program, one item each.

cwd.description: The folder a session of this profile starts in, unless the space or the tab names one. %NAME% is replaced by the environment variable NAME. In an SSH profile it is a folder on the other machine, taken as written, and when left out the home folder of the user there.

items.description: A shell profile of your own.

profiles.description: Shell profiles of your own, listed in the command palette after the ones Noren finds on the machine. An id the machine already has is refused when the profiles are loaded.

preset.description: Which set of shortcuts is in force: safe keeps the keys a shell uses, browser takes the keys of a web browser.

enabled.description: Off: Noren never asks the system to show a notification.

longCommandSeconds.description: A command that runs longer than this many seconds notifies when it ends out of sight.

enabled.description: Off: Noren never puts a tab in the archive on its own. A tab you archive or close yourself is not affected.

afterHours.description: How many hours a tab is left alone before it goes to the archive: with no command running, no output, nothing unread and not on screen. Pinned tabs and favorites are never archived. A fraction is fine (0.5 is half an hour).

archive.description: Auto-archive: tabs that nobody uses go to the archive with their saved output, and come back from the library.

enabled.description: Off: Noren never looks at the processes of your terminals and shows no agent icon.

resumeOnRestore.description: On: after the machine restarts, a tab that had an agent running (one whose catalog entry has a resume command, such as claude --continue) gets a new shell in its folder and that command is typed in it once, at the first prompt. Off: the tab only gets its shell back.

id.description: The name Noren shows for the agent. Unique in the catalog.

executables.description: File names of the program, without folder, ".exe" or ".cmd" (case does not matter): "claude" matches claude, Claude.exe and claude.cmd, and not claudette.

packages.description: Package names that identify the agent when it is started through a runner (node, npx, bunx, python, uv, pipx...): the runner counts as the agent when one of its arguments is the package, as in "npx pkg" or "python -m pkg".

working.description: Output that means the agent is working (a status line such as a spinner with its interrupt hint). Wins over idle, and is beaten by waiting.

waiting.description: Output that means the agent is asking you something (a permission question, a choice). The tab shows it as waiting for you. Without it, common yes/no questions count.

idle.description: Output that means the agent finished and is ready for your next message (its input prompt). Without it, silence is what makes the agent idle.

patterns.description: Regular expressions (case-insensitive, ^ and $ match at each line) tried on what the agent prints, with colors and cursor moves removed.

resume.description: The full command line that takes the agent up where it stopped, such as "claude --continue". Noren types it, once, in a new shell of a tab that had this agent running when the machine restarted, and only when agents.resumeOnRestore is on. Without it the agent is not resumed.

silenceSeconds.description: Seconds without output after which this agent counts as idle. Replaces agents.silenceSeconds for this agent.

items.description: A CLI agent Noren recognizes in a tab.

catalog.description: The CLI agents Noren recognizes in a tab, by the command being run and by the programs running under the shell. Replaces the built-in list when present, so copy the entries you want to keep.

scanSeconds.description: How many seconds between two looks at the process tree of the terminals, to find an agent that was not started from the prompt.

silenceSeconds.description: How many seconds an agent may print nothing before its tab shows it as idle. An agent entry can set its own.

agents.description: CLI agents: which programs count as an agent, how often Noren looks for one under your shells, and how the state of an agent (working, waiting for you, idle) is told. An agent shows as an icon on its tab.

enabled.description: Off: no AI function is offered and nothing is ever sent to a provider. A space can turn the AI off for itself too; it takes both being on.

id.description: The id of the provider, such as "my-openai". Unique among the providers; "ollama" is taken by the Ollama that Noren already knows. The API key is kept in the system keychain under this id.

kind.description: "openai-compatible" for Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM, OpenRouter, OpenAI, Groq and the like (the address is the API root, such as "https://api.openai.com/v1"); "anthropic" for the Anthropic API (such as "https://api.anthropic.com").

baseUrl.description: The address of the API, up to its root. Only http and https; never put a key in it, the key goes to the system keychain.

model.description: The model this provider uses when a function does not name one in ai.defaults.

items.description: An AI provider of your own.

providers.description: AI providers of your own, besides the Ollama on this computer that Noren already knows (id "ollama"). The API key of each is kept in the system keychain and never in this file.

provider.description: The id of a provider: "ollama" or one listed in ai.providers.

explain.description: For explaining the error of a command.

provider.description: The id of a provider: "ollama" or one listed in ai.providers.

command.description: For writing a command from a description.

provider.description: The id of a provider: "ollama" or one listed in ai.providers.

defaults.description: The provider and model each function uses by default (ask, explain, command). A function that is not listed has no default.

ai.description: The AI, off until you turn it on: providers (Ollama on this computer, and any you add) and which of them each function uses. Noren never runs what the AI suggests.

keepOnClose.description: On: closing the window leaves the shells of your panes running in the background (in the session daemon, norend) and opening Noren again gives each pane its shell back, with what it printed meanwhile. Off: closing the window ends every shell, as it always did. Shells that no pane comes back for are ended when Noren opens.

sessions.description: Whether the shells of your panes outlive the window.

method.description: How Pull, Push and the push on close sync your settings. "git": through the git remote connected in the Sync section of the settings. "gist": through a secret GitHub gist, with a token that lives in the system keychain. Each method keeps its own connection, so switching does not disconnect the other.

pushOnClose.description: On: closing Noren pushes to the connected git remote or gist first, when something is waiting to be sent (the settings file, themes, mods and spaces, the same files as Push in the settings). It waits a few seconds at most and never stops Noren from closing: a push that fails or is too slow is skipped. Off: Noren only syncs when you press Pull or Push.

sync.description: Sync of the settings through git or a gist: which one, and what Noren does on its own.

rules.description: The rules for a new tab, tried in the order of the file: the first one that matches decides the space (and the group). A rule with "cwd" and "command" needs both to match.

cwd.description: A glob for the whole folder of the tab: "*" is any characters inside one folder name, "**" is any number of folders, "?" is one character, "~" at the start is your home folder. "/" and "\" are the same on Windows, which also ignores upper and lower case. Write it with "/" to work on every system.

command.description: A regular expression (JavaScript syntax) for the line the tab runs: the profile and its arguments, as in "pwsh -NoLogo". It matches anywhere in the line; anchor it with ^ and $ to match the whole line.

space.description: The name of the space the tab goes to. A rule whose space does not exist is skipped.

group.description: The name of a group in that space to put the tab in. Without it the tab goes to the space itself. A rule whose group is not in the space is skipped.

routing.description: Where a new tab goes: rules that match the folder or the command of the tab and name a space and a group. A tab that no rule matches goes where it would have gone.

title: Noren settings
description: The settings file of Noren (config.jsonc). Every setting is optional.
